{{Short description|none}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox Hurling All-Ireland | year = 1967 | image = | dates = 14 May - 3 September 1967 | teams = 12 | connacht = | munster = Tipperary | leinster = Kilkenny | ulster = | matches = 11 | poty = [[Ollie Walsh]] | team = Kilkenny | titles = 16th | captain = [[Jim Treacy]] | manager = | team2 = Tipperary | captain2 = [[Mick Roche]] | manager2 = | totalgoals = | totalpoints = | topscorer = | previous = [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1966|1966]] | next = [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1968|1968]] }} The '''All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship of 1967''' was the 81st staging of [[Ireland]]'s premier [[hurling]] [[single-elimination tournament|knock-out competition]]. [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] won the championship, beating [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] 3–8 to 2–7 in the [[1967 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|final]] at [[Croke Park]], [[Dublin]]. ==Format== The All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship was run on a provincial basis as usual. All games were played on a knockout basis whereby once a team lost they were eliminated from the championship. The format for the All-Ireland series of games ran as follows: * There were no All-Ireland semi-finals. * The winners of the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] advanced directly to the All-Ireland final. * The winners of the [[Leinster Senior Hurling Championship|Leinster Championship]] advanced directly to the All-Ireland final. * The [[Ulster Senior Hurling Championship|Ulster Championship]] remained suspended due to a lack of competition. * [[Galway GAA|Galway]], a team who faced no competition in the [[Connacht Senior Hurling Championship|Connacht Championship]], played in the Munster Championship for the ninth consecutive year. ==Fixtures== ===[[Leinster Senior Hurling Championship]]=== {{footballbox |date=May 14, 1967
